vintage.pl_econ_champions: Curated 2026-11; figures 2017-2026 (each item has its year)

rules.made: Places behind products Poland is known for abroad, one fact each with the year of its figure. National figures are shown at one place that makes the product.
rules.tech: Tech companies at their main Polish office, the Polish TOP500 supercomputers (2026-11), satellite makers, the 2025 patent leader and the first cloud regions, one fact each.
rules.studios: Active video game studios on Wikidata with their headquarters in a Polish town and at least one released game; the best-known game is the one with the most Wikipedia articles, checked by hand for the largest studios. Studios in one town share one marker.

items.name: LG Energy Solution
items.fact: LG's electric-car battery plant now also makes grid storage: its first units went to PGE's Żarnowiec site in 2026-04.

items.name: Mercedes-Benz Jawor
items.fact: Four-cylinder engines and plug-in hybrid batteries for Mercedes plants worldwide, made by about 1,200 workers (2025-12). Large vans will be built here next.

items.name: Stellantis Tychy
items.fact: Tychy builds the Jeep Avenger, Fiat 600 and Alfa Romeo Junior. The 500,000th of these small SUVs left the line in 2026-06.

items.name: Toyota Jelcz-Laskowice
items.fact: Makes the 1.5 and 2.0 litre petrol engines for Toyota hybrids. Polish-made powertrains go into the Yaris, Corolla and C-HR built in Europe.

items.name: Toyota Wałbrzych
items.fact: With Jelcz-Laskowice, Toyota's first hybrid production centre outside Asia. Nearly 18 million powertrains have left its Polish plants since 2002.

items.name: Volkswagen Poznań
items.fact: The world's only maker of the VW Caddy: almost 103,000 left the Poznań plant in 2025.

items.name: Volkswagen Września
items.fact: The only plant that builds the VW Crafter: almost 70,000 in 2025, plus over 31,000 MAN TGE vans.

items.name: Newag
items.fact: Rail works since 1876, now maker of the Impuls electric trains. Record revenue in 2025: PLN 2.39 bn, up 50%.

items.name: PZL Mielec
items.fact: The 700th Black Hawk cabin was finished here in 2025-10. Some cabins go to the US, into UH-60M helicopters for the US Army.

items.name: Pesa
items.fact: Pesa finished 23 trams for Estonia in 2025. Revenue reached PLN 2.8 bn; new orders topped PLN 4.6 bn.

items.name: Solaris Bus & Coach
items.fact: Delivered 1,631 vehicles to 15 countries in 2025, 86% of them low- or zero-emission. Orders hit a record 2,780.

items.name: Galeon
items.fact: Galeon motor yachts are built here. Poland built about 25,000 boats in 2024 and led the EU in yacht exports in 2023 (USD 716.6 m).

items.name: Sunreef Yachts
items.fact: Luxury catamarans built in Gdańsk since 2002, first in the old Gdańsk Shipyard. Rafael Nadal's 80 Sunreef Power yacht was made in Gdańsk.

items.name: Drutex
items.fact: Poland is the world's top exporter of PVC windows and doors: about 36% of world exports (2021). Drutex in Bytów can make 7,000 a day.

items.name: Fakro
items.fact: Fakro calls itself the world's second-largest roof-window maker, with about 15% of the market (2025). Its research centre is in Nowy Sącz.

items.name: IKEA Industry Zbąszynek
items.fact: IKEA Industry's largest furniture factory in the world: about 45 million products in its last financial year, made by 3,400 workers.

items.name: LG Electronics Mława
items.fact: Almost 5,000 people work at LG's TV factory in Mława, opened in 1999. Many of LG's OLED TVs are assembled here.

items.name: Wronki appliance plants
items.fact: Poland makes 39% of the EU's large home appliances (2025). In Wronki, Amica builds cookers and Samsung builds fridges and washing machines.

items.name: Cedrob
items.fact: Poland is the EU's largest poultry producer: 2.9 million tonnes, 20.5% of EU output (2024). Cedrob, which calls itself Poland's largest, slaughters poultry here.

items.name: E. Wedel
items.fact: Wedel's chocolate factory has worked on ul. Zamoyskiego in Praga since 1931. Ptasie mleczko arrived in 1936. LOTTE has owned Wedel since 2010.

items.name: Grójec
items.label: Grójec orchards
items.fact: Poland grows 29% of the EU's apples, more than any other country (2024). The Grójec area is often called Europe's largest orchard.

items.name: Kraśnik
items.label: Raspberries
items.fact: Poland grows 45% of the EU's raspberries (2025). Lubelskie gives 71-83% of the Polish crop, and the area around Kraśnik is its raspberry hub.

items.name: Mowi Poland
items.fact: Mowi calls Mowi Poland, with 9 plants, its largest processing unit worldwide. One of its salmon plants stands here, near Ustka.

items.name: Żubrówka
items.fact: Żubrówka bison-grass vodka comes from a Białystok distillery founded in 1928. The grass grows in the Białowieża Forest; the brand says it is exported to over 40 countries.

items.name: Krosno
items.label: Krosno glass
items.fact: Krosno has made glass since 1923. Its glassware is now sold in 70 countries.

items.name: Muzeum Bursztynu
items.label: Amber Museum
items.fact: Gdańsk's city museum calls Gdańsk the World Capital of Amber. Its Amber Museum has filled the Great Mill since 2021.

items.name: Vitbis
items.label: Glass baubles
items.fact: Poland exported USD 31.5 m (PLN 124.8 m) of glass Christmas baubles in 2024, over half to the USA. Vitbis hand-blows them in Złotoryja.

items.name: Zakłady Ceramiczne Bolesławiec
items.label: Bolesławiec pottery
items.fact: Stoneware shaped and decorated by hand with sponge stamps. Zakłady Ceramiczne "Bolesławiec" have made it here since 1946 and offer almost 2,000 dishes.

items.name: Ćmielów
items.label: Ćmielów porcelain
items.fact: Porcelain made here since 1790. The firm that owns the Ćmielów and Chodzież factories makes 2,900 tonnes (8.5 million pieces) a year, sold in over 40 countries.

items.name: Inglot
items.fact: 95% of Inglot make-up is made in Przemyśl. The brand, founded in 1983, sells in 90 countries.

items.name: Ziaja
items.fact: Ziaja makes its cosmetics in two plants in Kolbudy. 2025 revenue was about PLN 500 m (EUR 115 m); exports bring just under a third.

items.name: Baltic Power
items.fact: Poland's first offshore wind farm lies 23 km off Choczewo: 76 turbines, up to 1.2 GW. First power reached the grid in 2026-07.

items.name: Grupa Azoty Puławy
items.fact: Grupa Azoty, owner of the Puławy nitrogen works, says it is the EU's second-largest maker of nitrogen and compound fertilisers (2025).

items.name: Blue Sunset Games
items.game: Go All Out: Free To Play

items.name: CD Projekt Red
items.fact: The Witcher 3 has sold over 65 million copies and Cyberpunk 2077 over 40 million. The whole Witcher series tops 90 million (2026).

items.name: Draw Distance
items.game: Vampire: The Masquerade – Coteries of New York

items.name: Simteract
items.game: Taxi Life: A City Driving Simulator

items.name: Allegro
items.fact: Allegro had 21 million active buyers in 2025, 15.3 million of them in Poland, choosing from over 80 million products.

items.name: Asseco Poland
items.fact: Rzeszów-based Asseco Group earned PLN 16.8 billion in 2025, and 86% of it came from outside Poland.

items.name: Booksy
items.fact: Polish-founded Booksy is used by over 346,000 beauty and wellness businesses in more than 50 countries (2026).

items.name: Brainly
items.fact: Brainly, a homework-help platform started in Poland in 2009, had about 15 million daily users in 2024.

items.name: Comarch
items.fact: Founded in Kraków in 1993, Comarch says brands in over 100 countries on six continents have used its software (2026).

items.name: Displate
items.fact: Displate, a Warsaw firm, had sold over 11 million metal posters to more than 1.8 million homes and offices by 2024-05.

items.name: Docplanner (ZnanyLekarz)
items.fact: Docplanner, known in Poland as ZnanyLekarz, booked 25 million doctor appointments in one month across 13 countries (2026).

items.name: ElevenLabs
items.fact: Founded in 2022 by two Poles, ElevenLabs was valued at $11 billion in 2026-02. In 2026-06 Poland's state bank BGK invested $11 million.

items.name: Huuuge Games
items.fact: Huuuge's games reach players in 174 countries in 32 languages. Its two casino titles averaged 282,100 daily players in 2025.

items.name: InPost
items.fact: InPost ran 28,165 parcel lockers in Poland at the end of 2025, and 61,196 across Europe.

items.name: Infermedica
items.fact: Wrocław's Infermedica runs AI symptom checks in 35 countries. Its Symptomate became the first app certified by Poland's health ministry in 2024.

items.name: Netguru
items.fact: Poznań's Netguru says it has delivered over 2,500 software projects since 2008, for clients such as IKEA, Volkswagen and Vinted.

items.name: Nomagic
items.fact: In 2025 Warsaw's Nomagic raised $44 million for AI robot arms that pick orders in warehouses for firms such as ASOS.

items.name: Ramp Network
items.fact: Founded in Warsaw in 2017, Ramp Network says over 10 million people have bought or sold crypto through its service.
items.seat_note: operating companies in London and Dublin

items.name: Synerise
items.fact: In 2025 the European Investment Bank lent Kraków AI firm Synerise EUR 25 million. The company says it operates in over 150 markets.

items.name: Text (LiveChat)
items.fact: Founded in Wrocław in 2002 as LiveChat, Text sells chat software to 30,000+ businesses in over 150 countries (2026).

items.name: Tidio
items.fact: Tidio, founded in Szczecin in 2013, says over 300,000 companies worldwide use its customer-service chat and AI agent (2026).

items.name: XTB
items.fact: Warsaw broker XTB won a record 864,000 new clients in 2025 and ended the year with over 2.16 million.

items.name: Beyond.pl
items.fact: The F.I.N, an AI supercomputer in Beyond.pl's commercial data centre, is number 252 in the world (TOP500, 2026-11), with 7.6 PFlop/s.

items.name: CI TASK Gdańsk
items.fact: Kraken-Fregata at CI TASK, Gdańsk University of Technology, is number 291 in the world (TOP500, 2026-11), with 6.0 PFlop/s.

items.name: Cyfronet AGH
items.fact: Helios GPU, number 54 in the world (TOP500, 2026-11), is Poland's fastest supercomputer at 53.6 PFlop/s. Cyfronet runs two more listed machines.

items.name: Google Cloud and Microsoft Azure
items.label: First cloud regions
items.fact: Google opened its first Polish cloud region in Warsaw in 2021-04. Microsoft's Azure Poland Central region followed in 2023-04.
items.seat_note: Data-centre sites are not public; the pin is Warsaw city centre. Microsoft says its region uses three locations around Warsaw.

items.name: PCSS Poznań
items.fact: Proxima at PCSS is number 156 in the world (TOP500, 2026-11), with 13.8 PFlop/s. PCSS also runs Altair, number 410.

items.name: WCSS Wrocław
items.fact: Lem at WCSS is number 173 in the world (TOP500, 2026-11), with 12.8 PFlop/s on Nvidia H100 GPUs.

items.name: CBK PAN
items.fact: GLOWS, built here, flies on NASA's IMAP probe; the science ministry calls it the first fully Polish research instrument. It recorded first light on 2025-11-13.

items.name: Creotech Instruments
items.fact: Creotech built EagleEye, launched in 2024-08, and says it is the first satellite over 50 kg designed and built in Poland.

items.name: KP Labs
items.fact: Intuition-1, launched in 2023-11, carries KP Labs' 192-band hyperspectral camera and an AI computer that analyses images in orbit.

items.name: SatRev
items.fact: SatRev built the platform of BlueBON, launched in 2025-01. SatRev says its camera had imaged over a million square kilometres of Earth by 2026-08.

items.name: Scanway
items.fact: Scanway builds space telescopes. In 2026-10 its two-telescope instrument, imaging Earth in visible and infrared light, switched on aboard South Korea's GYEONGGISat-2A.

items.name: Bielik (SpeakLeash)
items.fact: Bielik, a Polish language model with 11 billion parameters, was built by SpeakLeash and trained on Cyfronet's Helios and Athena supercomputers (2024).

items.name: Politechnika Lubelska
items.fact: Politechnika Lubelska won 128 Polish patents in 2025, more than any other applicant, Polish or foreign. Next: Politechnika Rzeszowska (108) and Warszawska (81).
